patterns.usage_note: A formal, written-style particle with two jobs: naming the means or grounds by which something is done (書類と面接をもって選考する), and naming the point at which something takes effect or ends (本日をもって). The second sense is what separates it from でもって, which stays instrumental. をもって is written and ceremonial; でもって is the one you may actually hear spoken. It is standard in notices, contracts and ceremonies; をもちまして is the extra-polite realization, and the fixed 身をもって ('through firsthand experience') keeps it alive in ordinary speech.

examples.ruby: 本日[ほんじつ]をもって当店[とうてん]は営業[えいぎょう]を終[お]えます。
examples.english: This shop will cease trading as of today.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]は身[み]をもって危険[きけん]を教[おし]えてくれた。
examples.english: He taught me how dangerous it was through his own hard experience.

examples.ruby: 選考[せんこう]は書類[しょるい]と面接[めんせつ]をもって行[おこな]います。
examples.english: Screening will be conducted on the basis of documents and an interview.
